expected_evidence: Geological/geochemical: platinum-group element (iridium/platinum) anomalies, magnetic and glassy microspherules, nanodiamonds, and 'black mat' organic layers in sediment cores dated to ~12,900 cal BP (Younger Dryas onset boundary), including the specific claimed occurrence in Lake Cuitzeo, Mexico sediment cores (model-prior: Israde-Alcántara et al. 2012 study)
Geological: a confirmed impact crater or airburst structure of appropriate age in or near Mexico/the Gulf region (none currently confirmed - model-prior)

Material/archaeological: megafaunal bone beds showing abrupt taphonomic extinction signature at the YD boundary layer, burn/charcoal spikes indicating continent-wide wildfires, Clovis-culture site disruption layers
Genetic: ancient-DNA-derived population bottleneck or extinction timing for North/Central American megafauna clustering sharply at ~12,900 BP rather than showing gradual decline

Astronomical: none directly recoverable (a discrete Pleistocene impact event leaves no observable astronomical record today; any 'astronomical' evidence would be indirect, e.g. modeled orbital debris streams - largely speculative)

Iconographic/oral_tradition/linguistic/textual: essentially none expected - no writing systems existed, and Paleolithic/PaleoIndian iconography or oral tradition from ~13,000 years ago is vanishingly unlikely to have transmitted intact to be recorded and identified as impact-related
response.rationale: The event date (~10,950 BCE) sits essentially at the Younger Dryas onset, so I applied the 'younger-dryas' row of the detectability table rather than the broader upper-paleolithic default. This hypothesis corresponds to the well-known Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (YDIH), and I recall (model-prior, unverified against the evidence text) that a specific study reported candidate impact markers (magnetic/glassy spherules, nanodiamonds) in a Lake Cuitzeo sediment core in Mexico dated to this interval - meaning the physical proxy evidence this hypothesis predicts has in fact reportedly been sought and partially reported in the actual target region, which raises confidence that such evidence, if real, is detectable with modern geochemical/sedimentological methods (geological: 0.65 in the table). However, the mechanism remains highly contested in the literature: no confirmed impact crater has been identified, and multiple independent labs have failed to replicate the spherule/nanodiamond signal at other YD-boundary sites, raising serious concern about contamination or misidentification (background terrestrial/cosmic dust vs. true impact ejecta). Material/faunal and genetic bottleneck evidence are moderately detectable (0.35, 0.3) but only weakly diagnostic of an impact specifically versus other extinction drivers (climate, human overkill, disease). Textual, linguistic, iconographic, and oral-tradition channels are essentially non-existent for this period/region and cannot inform confirmation or denial either way - their near-total absence (0.0-0.1) should not count as evidence against the hypothesis, only as an expected gap given the era. Overall, real evidence-seeking has occurred and produced contested-but-nonzero material, so the hypothesis is falsifiable-in-principle and not purely undetectable, but the mixed/disputed empirical record combined with the absence of a confirmed crater and low genetic/material specificity justifies a moderate (rather than high) detectability adjustment, well short of confirming the hypothesis as established.
